copy.gary: I've been wandering St. Pete parks for years and I still find something new on most visits, like a heron fishing off a seawall or a shady bench I'd walked past a hundred times.
copy.description: Check in at every St. Petersburg park you visit, collect stamps and badges, rate your favorites and explore with your Park Pals.
copy.og_alt: Parks Passport: stamp every St. Pete park you visit. Gary the park guide waves in front of the St. Pete Pier at sunrise.

motifs.name: Sunshine City
motifs.blurb: From 1910 the Evening Independent gave the paper away free on any day the sun didn't shine. St. Pete later logged 768 sunny days in a row.

motifs.name: Brown pelican
motifs.blurb: Brown pelicans work the bay and the pier all year, folding their wings to dive bill-first for fish.

motifs.name: The Pier
motifs.blurb: A pier has reached into Tampa Bay here since the 1889 Railroad Pier. Today's 26-acre St. Pete Pier opened in 2020.

motifs.name: Green benches
motifs.blurb: In the early 1900s thousands of green benches lined downtown sidewalks. They were the city's emblem until they were removed in the 1960s.

motifs.name: Shuffleboard
motifs.blurb: The St. Petersburg Shuffleboard Club, founded in 1924 next to Mirror Lake, is one of the oldest in the world.

motifs.name: Tampa Bay sailing
motifs.blurb: Downtown's waterfront parks face Tampa Bay, where sailboats have crossed the skyline since the city's earliest days.

motifs.name: Mangroves
motifs.blurb: Weedon Island Preserve protects more than 3,000 acres of mangroves on Tampa Bay, once home to the Weeden Island culture.

motifs.name: Waterfront palms
motifs.blurb: Palms frame the chain of waterfront parks that runs along downtown's bayfront, one of the longest public waterfronts in the country.

motifs.name: SHINE murals
motifs.blurb: Since 2015 the SHINE Mural Festival has painted hundreds of walls, turning the city into an open-air gallery.
